candidate.answerReason: There are 55 residents of A, 40 residents of B, and 20 residents of C who work in A. Their total is 115.

methods.label: Count workers by home city
methods.explanation:
Count the people who work in \(A\) according to where they live. Each arrow's fraction applies to the population of the city where the arrow starts.

The arrows leaving \(A\) show that \(\frac14\cdot100=25\) residents work in \(B\), and \(\frac15\cdot100=20\) work in \(C\). Since everyone works in exactly one of the three cities, the number who both live and work in \(A\) is
\[
100-25-20=55.
\]
The arrows pointing into \(A\) show that \(\frac13\cdot120=40\) residents of \(B\) and \(\frac18\cdot160=20\) residents of \(C\) work there.

These three groups include everyone who works in \(A\), and no person belongs to two groups because each person has one home city. Therefore the total is
\[
55+40+20=\boxed{115},
\]
which is choice \(\text{D}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses fractions of whole-number populations and addition and subtraction of disjoint groups.

review.mathematicalCheck: The actual arrows confirm the four fractions used. A contributes 100-25-20=55 workers, B contributes 120/3=40, and C contributes 160/8=20. These disjoint home-city groups exhaust everyone working in A, totaling 115.
